# HEmptyState

> An inviting first-run or no-results state, with room for a useful next action.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.5.1. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HEmptyState` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-empty-state>`.
- Constructor: `HearthEmptyStateElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Feedback.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HEmptyState.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Use for first-run or no-results states, with one useful next action in the default slot.
- Use HSkeleton for content that is still loading, and HAlert for a problem that requires attention.

## Public API

title, description, icon: string

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    title?: string;
    description?: string;
    icon?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ title: "Your next chapter starts here.", icon: "apps" }
```

### Events

None

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

default (actions)

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, icon, title, description

Use `hearth-empty-state::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HEmptyState, HButton } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
function add() { /* Open your creation flow. */ }
</script>

<template>
  <HEmptyState title="Your trail starts here." description="Add an application to build your dashboard." icon="apps">
    <HButton variant="primary" @click="add">Add application</HButton>
  </HEmptyState>
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-empty-state');
Object.assign(element, {
  "title": "Your trail starts here.",
  "description": "Add an application to build your dashboard.",
  "icon": "apps"
});

element.innerHTML = "<hearth-button variant=\"primary\">Add application</hearth-button>"; // Static example markup only; never inject untrusted HTML.

mount.append(element);
```

## Related components

- [HSkeleton](../skeleton/llms.txt): Text, rectangle, and circular loading placeholders with reduced-motion support.
- [HAlert](../alert/llms.txt): Inline feedback for success, information, and problems. Errors announce as alerts; other tones use status.
- [HButton](../button/llms.txt): Native button or link behavior, clear focus, icon-only labels, and restrained press feedback.
